domain_analysis.scope: Interior new construction stair railing system stain and clear coat for wood components
domain_analysis.workflow_overview: Three-layer coating system on multi-component railing: stain > sealer > clear. Baluster count is dominant labor driver. Canonical sequence: balusters > newels > handrails. Wood-only scope (iron balusters use paint, not stain).
key_differences_from_paint_counterpart: Wood-only — no iron/metal substrate handling (iron uses paint)
No primer — stain spec handles all layers from bare wood
Three product roles (stain, sealer, clear) vs one (finish)
Wipe step critical for baluster detail — turned balusters require intricate wipe
No substrate_state dimension — always SS_BARE for stain (no powder coat, no factory prime)
railing_style replaces baluster_profile for simpler modifier set
key_differences_from_trim_stain: Multi-item spec: 3 paintable items with different UOMs
Baluster count drives majority of labor
Mandatory tread protection at all times
Spray more practical for spindle work than for flat trim

key_rates.railing_stain_brush: ~60 LF/hr — stain + wipe on handrail (4 surfaces). ~1 min per LF.
key_rates.baluster_stain_brush: ~6-8 min/EA — intricate wipe for turned profiles. Simple square ~4 min/EA.
key_rates.baluster_stain_spray: ~4-5 min/EA — spray + wipe. Better coverage on turned profiles.

risk_notes.risk: Inconsistent wipe on 39+ balusters creates visible color variation
risk_notes.mitigation: Consistent timing. Wipe in sections. Same person does all balusters.

risk_notes.risk: Clear runs/drips on vertical spindle surfaces
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats. Watch for drips at baluster-to-handrail junction. Spray gives more even coverage.
Mandatory heavy tread protection. Verify protection integrity before each coat.

assumptions.value: Stain spec covers wood railings only. Iron/metal balusters require paint (SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC), not stain.
In a typical 39-baluster system, balusters represent ~65-70% of total stain/clear labor.
